flawed_step: Line 0010 multiplies by g(n) without establishing that g(n)>0, so the inequality need not be preserved.
counterexample: Let g(n)=-1 and f(n)=-n. Then f(n)/g(n)=n→∞. However, multiplying n>M by g(n)=-1 reverses the inequality: f(n)=-n<-M=M g(n), not f(n)>M g(n). Moreover, for every c1>0, 0≤c1g(n) is false because c1g(n)=-c1<0, so the claimed Ω relation does not follow.
assessment_summary: The statement and proof need an eventual positivity assumption on g (and the usual nonnegativity conditions on asymptotic functions). As written, the explicit counterexample refutes the relied-upon multiplication step and the claimed conclusion.
